# Recommended Reading  {.unnumbered}

- **Freedman, D., Pisani, R., & Purves, R. (2007). _Statistics_ (4th ed.). W. W. Norton.**  
  Emphasizes conceptual understanding of estimation and uncertainty. Especially strong on interpreting standard errors, margins of error and tests of significance.

- **Lakens, D. (2022). _Improving Your Statistical Inferences_.**  
  A free online textbook written for psychologists, covering p-values, error rates, power, effect sizes and confidence intervals, with many interactive examples.  
  [https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/](https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/)

- **Cumming, G. (2012). _Understanding the New Statistics: Effect Sizes, Confidence Intervals, and Meta-Analysis_. Routledge.**  
  Argues for estimation (effect sizes with confidence intervals) rather than significance testing alone, with examples from psychology.
